$comment:
THE ASCENT GATE, AND THE STUB THE PLAYER MUST NOT WALK INTO. Stages 6 to 8 are not built, and the honest way to say so is not an invisible wall: it is a gate that has been open every day for nine hundred years, shut this week, with a warden in front of it who will tell you exactly why and exactly what would change it. Everything he says is true inside Act 5 and stays true when Stage 7 opens the road -- nothing here has to be retracted later.

WRAPPED BY THE ASCENT BUILD, ADDITIVELY. Everything below the else is the original scene, unchanged: this man is the stub that told the player why Stages 6 to 8 were not there yet, and inside Act 5 he still is. The new branch is what he says once `summit_open` is set and the gate behind him is standing open -- he is a sixth-generation gatekeeper who has just had to shut it for the first time in his family's history, and the beat is him getting to open it again. He does not congratulate the player on saving the region. Nobody on this road does.

lines: Six days. Six days shut, and my mother never shut it once in forty years.
It went back on the hook this morning and I have not stopped looking at it.
Four miles. Ford at the second fall, and the bridge is still out, so wade it.
There is a bothy above the cloud. Stop at it. Everyone thinks they will not need to.
My cousin has the gate at the top. Tell her I said the road is clear.
On you go, {name}. Nobody has ever hurried on this road either.
Eight. Right. I am going to write your name in the book and then I am going to shut it again.
Not you. The gate. It has been shut for six days and it is going to stay shut.
Four miles of road and half of it is above the snow line. Wind on it like a hand.
I have put people up that road in bad weather before. I am not doing it in this.
When it turns, we post it in the yard and the whole city knows in an hour.
Go and do whatever it is you are actually here for, {name}. This will keep.
Shut. Weather. No exceptions, and I have said that eleven hundred times this week.
Come back with eight and I will still say it, so do not hurry on my account.
My mother had this post. Her father had it. Neither of them ever shut it.
There is a tally board behind you with a nought on it. I had to chalk over the nought.

$comment: TARIN AT CROWNSPIRE, AND THE AGREEMENT ABOUT THE SUMMIT. Canon: at Crownspire they agree that once Meridian is finished, they both go up. His Crest count is owned by src/systems/tarin.ts and this scene does not assume a number -- it asks tarin_holds_8, then tarin_holds_7, and falls through to a line that is true whatever the ledger says, so it cannot break if the ledger owner lands a different beat. It sets cs_summit_pact for the ledger and for Stage 7 to read; nothing here sets a tarin_* flag, because those are derived and setFlag cannot touch them. He is standing at the foot of the Crown Stair looking up it, and he makes exactly one joke in the whole scene, before the pact rather than after it.

lines: Still shut. I check at six and I check at four, and it is still shut.
Doesn't matter. We know where we are going. Go and finish the other thing.
Eight. You have got eight.
I have been standing at the bottom of these steps for two days working out what to say.
So have I. Took me four goes at Ord and I am not going to pretend it was three.
Which means there is nothing left between either of us and that road up there.
Seven. I go up to Ord tomorrow and I am going to lose to her at least twice first.
I am fine about it. I am saying it out loud so that I stay fine about it.
I am behind you. Again. I have decided to find that funny this time.
I will get there. That has never been the part I was worried about.
He looks up the Crown Stair for a while, at the terrace, and past it at the shut gate.
Somewhere above all of it there is a mountain, and today there is only weather where it should be.
I could go up on my own, you know. The moment they open it. I have thought about it.
I am not going to. Meridian first. Whatever that turns out to mean, and I know it is bad.
And then the Summit, and we go up the same morning. Both of us. Say yes.
The same morning. Both of you.
Right. Good. That is that settled and I am not going to make a thing of it.
You are going to say yes eventually, so I am writing it down as a yes.
I have been right about this since we were eleven.
Four thousand one hundred and nine names on that wall and not one of them went up as a pair.
I looked. Two days, and I looked at all of them.
They are cutting yours in the yard, by the way. I went and watched.
I am going to be so unbearable about mine. Fair warning.
Ord is up there. Go on. I want to hear what she does to you.
That came out wrong. I want to hear how it went.
Two days I have been in this square. You take your time, don't you.
I have been up to the gate every morning at six. Every morning it is shut.
There is a man there whose family has held the post for three generations and he is frightened.
It does not rain here, {name}. Not in summer. The Archive has nine hundred years of noughts.
Everybody in this city is talking about the weather and nobody is talking about the weather.
Go and take the eighth off Ord. Walk her gallery first - the whole of it, both sides.
I did not, the first time. She let me not, which was worse.

$comment:
THE FOOT OF THE ASCENT, and the join the Ascent build could not make from its own side: Registry.loadScriptsFor only fetches data/events/<mapId>.json, so a trigger on Crownspire's paving has to live in Crownspire's array. Nothing above this line is touched and data/maps/crownspire.json is not touched at all.

WHERE. The four cells of the gate arch at 46-49,4, which are GRANITE_ARCH and already walkable, with solid wall above them -- so before this script the arch was an alcove a player could stand in and nothing else. The warden stands at 47,5 and blocks one of the four approaches, which is correct and does not need changing.

THE GATE. `summit_open`, set by aftermath_summit in data/events/aureline_summit.json, whose own note says it is the flag Stage 7 should hang the Ascent on. A step script whose `when` fails does nothing at all (EventRunner.start), so through the whole of Act 5 these four cells stay exactly what they were and the warden's tally board keeps its number.

WHERE IT LANDS. data/maps/ascent_road.json, 34-35,54 -- the paved apron on the far side of the same gate, drawn out of Crownspire's own granite and its own arch so that the seam is one gate seen from two sides. The road warps back at its own 34-35,55 to crownspire 48,5 and 49,5, which are open paving; 47,5 is deliberately not used because the warden is standing on it.

lines: Two leaves of oak in an iron frame, standing open for the first time in six days.
The plank that was nailed across them is leaning against the wall with the nails still in it.

$comment2: NO EXPLICIT FADES. EventHost.warp does its own eighteen-frame fade out, load and fade in, and a fade action either side of it is a second fade fighting the first.
